content.heading: 6.3.1. Shortening dual antiplatelet therapy
content.summary: Several RCTs and meta-analyses compared standard 12-month DAPT with shorter (≈3–6 month) regimens followed by aspirin or P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy in ACS patients. Shortened DAPT reduced bleeding but some abbreviated regimens (eg, 3-month) were associated with higher ischaemic events (MI or stent thrombosis) in some analyses. Trials investigating very short DAPT (≈1–3 months) then P2Y12 monotherapy included patients at low-to-intermediate ischaemic risk; STEMI patients tended to be excluded or under-represented.
key_findings: Large network meta-analysis: 3-month DAPT (but not 6-month) associated with higher rates of MI or stent thrombosis in ACS patients.
Several large RCTs investigated 1–3 months DAPT followed by P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy (clopidogrel or ticagrelor) in patients with and without ACS.
TWILIGHT: ticagrelor monotherapy after 3 months DAPT reduced clinically relevant bleeding without signal for increased ischaemic risk in selected high‑risk patients.
TICO: ticagrelor monotherapy after 3 months DAPT tested in ACS patients showed reduced net adverse clinical events and major bleeding in the trial population tested.
STOPDAPT-2-ACS: investigated very short DAPT strategies in ACS; non-inferiority for composite CV/bleeding endpoints was not proven for very short (<3 months) DAPT followed by clopidogrel monotherapy.

trials_reported.name: TWILIGHT
trials_reported.description: Examined ticagrelor monotherapy vs ticagrelor+aspirin after 3 months of DAPT in high‑risk patients; reduced BARC type 2–5 bleeding without signal of increased ischaemic risk.

trials_reported.name: TICO
trials_reported.description: Tested ticagrelor monotherapy vs ticagrelor+aspirin after 3 months DAPT in ACS patients (3056 patients); showed reductions in net adverse clinical events and major bleeding.

trials_reported.name: STOPDAPT-2-ACS
trials_reported.description: Investigated short DAPT strategy in ACS patients; at ~2 months patients randomized to clopidogrel monotherapy vs 12 months DAPT; non-inferiority was not proven for the composite CV/bleeding endpoint.

content.clinical_implication: Shortened DAPT (particularly transitioning to P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy after 3 months) can reduce bleeding in selected populations, but selection of patients (ischaemic risk, STEMI status) is critical and very short DAPT (<3 months) may not be appropriate in ACS.

Associated Conditions: Target of P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (antiplatelet therapy)
Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) / patients treated with coronary stents
genes.context: Text refers to 'P2Y12 receptor inhibitor monotherapy' as the strategy after shortened DAPT in patients with and without ACS (i.e., use of P2Y12 receptor antagonists such as clopidogrel or ticagrelor).
